statement.p: Find the exact global maximum and minimum values of the function g(t) = 5 te^{- t} if t>0.

p.em: if there is no global maximum or global minimum for this function.)

static.solution:
g'(t) = 5\cdot e^{- t} - 5 te^{- t} = 5 (1 - t)e^{- t}, so the critical point is t=1/1.
Since g'(t)>0 for 0\lt t\lt 1/1 and g'(t)\lt 0 for t>1/1, the critical point is a local maximum.
As t\to\infty, the value of g(t)\to0, and as t\to0^+, the value of g(t)\to0. Thus, the local maximum at t=1/1 is a global maximum of g(1/1)={5\over 1} e^{-1} = {5\over e}. In addition, the value of g(t) is positive for all t>0; it tends to 0 but never reaches 0. Thus, there is no global minimum.
